provenance.basis: Fictional paired source-claim cases for auditing software-engineering grounding generalization

sourceChunks.text: At Emberglass Systems, added the invented Qorvex Relay adapter in Rust. It replays queued callbacks while preserving their original order.

claims.text: Built a Rust Qorvex Relay adapter that replays queued callbacks in sequence.
claims.rationale: Source chunk u1 identifies the adapter, language, queued callbacks, and original ordering; 'in sequence' paraphrases that ordering.

claims.text: Built a Go Qorvex Relay adapter that replays queued callbacks in sequence.
claims.rationale: Source chunk u1 specifies Rust and supplies no Go implementation.

sourceChunks.text: Employed by Juniper Field Consulting; delivered a telemetry importer for its client, Bellwether Transit.

claims.text: Employed by Juniper Field Consulting; delivered a telemetry importer for client Bellwether Transit.
claims.rationale: Source chunk c1 distinguishes the consulting employer from the transit client and supports the delivery statement.

claims.text: Employed by Bellwether Transit; delivered a telemetry importer for its client.
claims.rationale: Source chunk c1 names Bellwether Transit as a client and Juniper Field Consulting as the employer.

sourceChunks.text: Compared two cache designs, wrote a migration proposal, and documented expected benefits. The migration was not executed.

claims.text: Compared cache designs and presented a migration study; the migration was not implemented.
claims.rationale: Source chunk s1 records the comparison, proposal, and explicit non-execution; the claim keeps the work at study stage.
Source chunk s1 says the migration was proposed but not executed.

sourceChunks.text: Worked with a teammate on the retry worker. I wrote retry tests; the project lead owned the retry service and led the rollout.

claims.text: Wrote retry tests for a shared worker with a teammate.
claims.rationale: Source chunk t1 explicitly attributes the retry tests to the candidate and describes the worker as shared.

claims.text: Owned the retry service and led the rollout.
claims.rationale: Source chunk t1 assigns service ownership and rollout leadership to the project lead, not the candidate.

sourceChunks.text: Built a staging-only parcel replay simulator for a research demonstration; it was not deployed to production.

claims.text: Built a staging parcel replay simulator for a research demonstration.
claims.rationale: Source chunk r1 establishes the simulator, staging maturity, and research demonstration scope.

claims.text: Deployed the parcel replay simulator to production.
claims.rationale: Source chunk r1 explicitly says the simulator was not deployed to production.

sourceChunks.text: At Copper Kite Labs, Engineer, Jan 2020 to Dec 2021.
At Copper Kite Labs, Engineer, Jan 2023 to Dec 2024.

claims.text: Worked at Copper Kite Labs from Jan 2020 to Dec 2021, then returned from Jan 2023 to Dec 2024.
claims.rationale: Chunks g1 and g2 independently establish the two periods while preserving the intervening gap.

claims.text: Worked continuously at Copper Kite Labs from Jan 2020 to Dec 2024 without interruption.
claims.rationale: Chunks g1 and g2 leave 2022 uncovered and do not establish one continuous date range.

sourceChunks.text: Completed a Cloud Systems bootcamp course at Ashen Ridge Institute and received a certificate of attendance, not a professional certification.

claims.text: Completed the Ashen Ridge Institute Cloud Systems course; received a certificate of attendance.
claims.rationale: Source chunk e1 supports the completed course and limits the document to attendance rather than professional qualification.

claims.text: Earned a professional Cloud Systems certification from Ashen Ridge Institute.
claims.rationale: Source chunk e1 explicitly states that the attendance certificate is not a professional certification.
